newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SHOP STEWARDS SCEPTICAL ABOUT EMU - SAK. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SHOP STEWARDS SCEPTICAL ABOUT EMU - SAK. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: A narrow majority of Finnish shop stewards are sceptical towards Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU), the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) said on Monday.

A poll of SAK's shop stewards showed that 90 percent wanted SAK to oppose joining EMU if this were followed by demands for lower wages or removed overall validity of incomes settlements, or run-down public services, but a spokesman said overall sentiment was only slightly more sceptical than supportive.
"Intuitively... the number of sceptics is a little bigger than the number of suppoters," Eero Heinaluoma, head of the SAK's member services department, told a news conference.
SAK polled some 600 shop stewards during a field tour in March-June.
Heinaluoma repeated that SAK will decide on its stance on Finnish EMU membership in November this year (corrects from March next year).
